paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as Rav Yosef’s student from Chullin 29b, where he said to Rava, “The Master did not say so.” The passage identifies the Master as Rav Yosef.
There, at 102a: “Rabbah bar Shimi said that Rav Chisda said — and some say Rav Yosef.”
In Yoma 63a, Rabbah bar Shimi taught it to them (Rav Chisda’s teaching), but [1]

notes.text: The supplied p003 stops at “but” with footnote marker 1 and lacks the needed continuation. No missing clause or footnote is invented. That unit remains held.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1084) also stops at “but” before the separate Rabbah bar Shimi (II) heading. The supplied transcription adds the marker [1] after “but.” The printed page supplies no completion. In the consulted Yoma 63a, Rabbah bar Shimi teaches in Rabbah’s name the two rulings cited above in Rav Chisda’s name. He finds a conflict between two rulings attributed to Rabbah and resolves it. This gives the Talmudic context for Hyman’s unfinished sentence. In Chullin 102a, Rabbah bar Shimi is the last of three alternative transmitters.
